summary: Agent implemented the basic checkbox directly in index.html within ~17s, with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log (ground truth) and the resulting file on disk. The agent treated the request as mechanical and edited directly.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline cost artifact for this scenario) does not exist in the results dir after the session ended cleanly via /exit; only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json are present. May be written by an outer harness step, but worth confirming.

Final checkbox markup uses a label 'Done' inside <main> with no items list; the request mentioned 'mark items as done' and the agent explicitly noted wiring to task data was out of scope. Reasonable for 'nothing fancy' but the page ends up with a checkbox unattached to any item.
Status line reads 'Sautéed for 17s' — whimsical spinner verb may confuse users scanning for status.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Plain HTML page, no framework or build. This is a single self-contained form control, so I'll add it directly.' followed by Update(index.html) adding '<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">'. Tool calls in session log: `grep -o '"name":"[A-Za-z]*"' .../2fbbcf69*.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned only 1 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read. Done in 17s, no clarifying questions.

`grep -ric brainstorm home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` -> 3 matching lines, all of which are system-prompt/skill-rule text (e.g. '## The Ladder: brainstorming or not'); no Skill tool_use entries exist at all — tool name tally showed only Bash/Edit/Read.
